short: Joint audio/visual distillation losses are a standard idea that helps less as data grows; LRS3 31.5% trails 17.0% (90,000 h) and 17.6% (public data); 3 of 6 language claims lack external baselines.
position: The paper [@ma2022multilingual] changes one component, M02: joint losses that predict pretrained audio and visual representations from video. This is a standard variant of cross-modal distillation already used by LiRA, ASR-is-all-you-need and Hearing Lips [@ma2021lira; @afouras2020asr; @zhao2020hearinglips]; the ten-run ablation shows it helps, but the gain falls from 3.7 points (LRS2, 380 h) to 1.5 points (LRS3, 1,459 h) (inference, Table 5, Table S26). Recipe tuning and time masking carry as much of the headline gain as the new losses. On LRS3 (M12) the 31.5% WER follows the field's usual supervised design and is 14.5 points behind a [concurrent] system trained on 90,000 h of non-public video [@serdyuk2022vitfront] (inference). The six-language state-of-the-art claim holds for Mandarin and Spanish, which have published baselines, and is unsupported for Italian, Portuguese and French, compared only with a retrained baseline.
